title: Independence Palace (Reunification Convention Hall)
text: Independence Palace is located at 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1. It served as the home and workplace of the President of South Vietnam before 1975. The palace is open daily to visitors from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. General admission tickets for the main building are 40,000 VND for adults and 20,000 VND for students. Guided tours and multilingual automated audio guides are available on site.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Historical Landmarks

title: Ben Thanh Market
text: Ben Thanh Market is situated in central District 1 with four main gates facing major streets. The South Gate, featuring a three-sided clock tower, is an iconic symbol of Saigon. The market operates daily from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM with stalls selling souvenirs, fabrics, local coffee, and Vietnamese regional specialties. After 6:00 PM, the side streets turn into a bustling night market. Bargaining is recommended when shopping for dry goods and souvenirs.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Shopping and Dining

title: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon
text: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica is located at Paris Square (Cong xa Paris), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1. Built in the late 19th century, the cathedral combines Romanesque and Gothic architectural styles, with all exterior red bricks imported directly from Marseille, France. The cathedral is currently undergoing major restoration, so visitors can only admire and photograph the exterior grounds free of charge.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Architectural Heritage

title: Saigon Central Post Office
text: Located right next to Notre-Dame Cathedral at 2 Paris Square, the Saigon Central Post Office was designed by French architects Auguste Henri Villedieu and Alfred Foulhoux in the late 19th century. The building features grand arched vaults, classic tiled flooring, and historic painted wall maps. Admission is free, and it is open on weekdays and Saturdays from 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM, and Sundays from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, offering active postal services and souvenir postcards.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Architectural Heritage

title: War Remnants Museum
text: Located at 28 Vo Van Tan Street, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, this is one of the most visited museums in Vietnam. It houses extensive exhibits of authentic photographs, military aircraft, tanks, weapons, and documentary evidence detailing the Vietnam War and the humanitarian impact of Agent Orange. The museum is open daily from 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Admission ticket is 40,000 VND per person.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Museums and History

title: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
text: Nguyen Hue Walking Street extends from the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Building to Bach Dang Wharf in District 1. Paved entirely with granite, the street is closed to motorized vehicles on Saturday and Sunday evenings from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM for pedestrians and street performances. Visitors can explore the trendy cafe apartments at 42 Nguyen Hue, tea shops, and vibrant open-air music shows.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Entertainment and Urban Life

title: Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens
text: Established in 1864 at 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, the Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens is one of the oldest zoos in the world. It is home to hundreds of rare animal species and a lush canopy of heritage trees. Opening hours are daily from 7:00 AM to 5:30 PM. Ticket prices are 60,000 VND for visitors 1.3 meters and above, 40,000 VND for children between 1.0 and 1.3 meters, and free for children under 1.0 meter.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Nature and Parks

title: Cu Chi Tunnels
text: The Cu Chi Tunnels are located approximately 70 kilometers northwest of central Ho Chi Minh City, with two main public visiting sectors at Ben Duoc and Ben Dinh. This legendary underground network spans over 250 kilometers of interconnected tunnels, command bunkers, living quarters, and field hospitals used during the war. Open daily from 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Admission is approximately 35,000 VND for domestic visitors and 125,000 VND for international visitors.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Historical Landmarks

title: Ba Thien Hau Pagoda (Chinatown - Cho Lon)
text: Ba Thien Hau Pagoda (Tue Thanh Assembly Hall) is located at 710 Nguyen Trai Street, Ward 11, District 5. Established in the 18th century by the Cantonese Chinese community in Saigon, the pagoda is dedicated to Thien Hau, Goddess of the Sea. Notable features include intricate porcelain dioramas on the roof, large hanging spiral incense coils, and sacred historic altars. The temple is open daily from 6:00 AM to 5:00 PM with free entrance.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Culture and Spirituality

title: Landmark 81 and Vinhomes Central Park
text: Landmark 81 is located at 720A Dien Bien Phu Street, Ward 22, Binh Thanh District, and stands as the tallest skyscraper in Vietnam. The Vincom Center shopping mall is open freely from 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM. The SkyView Observation Deck on floors 79 to 81 operates from 8:30 AM to 10:00 PM with standard adult tickets priced at approximately 420,000 VND. Adjacent to the tower is the 14-hectare riverside Central Park with pedestrian bridges and expansive green spaces.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Modern Landmarks

title: Bui Vien Walking Street
text: Centered along Bui Vien, De Tham, and Pham Ngu Lao streets in District 1, Bui Vien is famous as Saigon's premier nightlife hub. The street turns pedestrian-only from 7:00 PM to 2:00 AM on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday nights. Visitors can enjoy chilled local draft beers, street snacks, outdoor music lounges, and an energetic multicultural crowd.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Nightlife and Entertainment

title: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
text: Located at 97A Pho Duc Chinh Street, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, this museum occupies the former mansion of merchant Hui Bon Hoa. The yellow mansion harmoniously combines French Art Deco architecture with traditional Chinese elements and houses the oldest operational elevator in Saigon. Open daily from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Admission ticket is 30,000 VND for adults and 15,000 VND for students.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Arts and Culture

title: Alley 200 Xom Chieu Food Street (District 4)
text: Alley 200 Xom Chieu in Ward 14, District 4 is widely regarded as one of Saigon's finest street food havens. Stretching roughly 500 meters, the alley hosts dozens of vibrant food stalls operating daily from 4:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Popular dishes include beef offal stew (pha lau), grilled banana in coconut milk, fresh shellfish, and crab soup, with affordable prices ranging between 20,000 and 50,000 VND per portion.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Culinary Culture

title: Bach Dang Wharf and Saigon Waterbus
text: Bach Dang Wharf is located along Ton Duc Thang Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, offering a scenic riverside park looking across to the Thu Thiem peninsula. From Bach Dang Station, passengers can take the public Saigon Waterbus cruising upriver to Linh Dong Station in Thu Duc. It provides an exceptional sunset view over the city skyline. A one-way ticket costs 15,000 VND per person; booking in advance is advised on weekends.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - River Experiences

title: Ho Thi Ky Flower and Street Food Market
text: Located in alley networks off Ward 1, District 10, Ho Thi Ky is the largest wholesale fresh flower market in Ho Chi Minh City, operating 24 hours a day with blooms from Da Lat and the Mekong Delta. From 3:00 PM until midnight, the market area transforms into a celebrated street food street famous for Cambodian snacks such as sweet dessert soups, grilled Cambodian sausages, and num bo chok noodles, priced from 15,000 to 45,000 VND.
source: Lumen Travel Guide Ho Chi Minh City - Shopping and Dining
